newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB says idea of Suez/Lyonnaise merger exists.
newsitem.headline: SGB says idea of Suez/Lyonnaise merger exists.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) said on Wednesday the notion of a merger between its parent Cie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux existed, but no decision had been taken on it at a board level.

"It is a fact that the board of Suez has not discussed (the possibility of a merger)...the hypothesis does exist, however, but no decision has been taken about it," SGB chairman Etienne Davignon said in reply to questions at a news conference on 1996 earnings.
He declined to say at what level talks about the merger had been held.

But he said that for instance the merger between SGB units Tractebel and Powerfin, announced on Tuesday, had been discussed for two years between himself and Tractebel executives before a formal proposal was made to the boards of the respective companies.
"To discuss something is one thing. It does not mean it is immediately put to the board. Once you go to the board you have to come up with a concrete proposal."

He said he had gone to Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene to explain the possible impact in Belgium of such a merger. Belgian authorities had expressed concern about the effect on utility Tractebel of a merger with Lyonnaise.
